next_step: Closed-lost to OpenAI; add to nurture list, send post-mortem recap + benchmark invite
closed_lost_reason: Chose OpenAI direct API for perceived simplicity/brand trust; procurement cited speed to market and existing OpenAI credits
notes:
Overview: Mid-market ecommerce platform evaluating conversational and search features for merchant support and product discovery. Team enthusiastic about latency and embeddings improvements but ultimately opted for direct OpenAI integration.

Timeline / Recent activity:
- 2024-06-20: Intro call (Jordan) — high level use cases, buyer group: Product + Infra + Security.
- 2024-07-02: Discovery workshop with Product (Fireflies id ff_20250721_ambercore_demo). Collected sample docs, search queries.
- 2024-08-15: Technical deep-dive with SE (Anita) — discussed caching, batching, model routing, Dedicated option.
- 2024-09-03: POC kickoff — small evaluation cluster (hosted). Provided sample prompts and eval harness.
- 2024-10-10: Security review — requested SOC2 details, retention controls. Redwood provided security FAQ + drive link.
- 2025-01-22: Pricing negotiation — AmberCore pushed for lower per-token tiers; finance concerned about multi-region costs.
- 2025-03-11: Procurement signalled preference for fastest path to production. AmberCore had internal tests with OpenAI and liked the simplicity of direct API calls.
- 2025-06-30: Internal champion (Lead PM) moved to new role; momentum slowed.
- 2025-10-28: Final procurement call — AmberCore confirmed selection of OpenAI direct APIs citing brand trust and pre-existing credits. Closed-lost 2025-11-03.

Key requirements / priorities from buyer:
- Workload: chat support bot (low-latency), enterprise search (embeddings), product recommendations (reranking).
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms for chat.
- Throughput: steady 150 requests/s peak expected (burst to 400 for sale events).
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — looking for predictable unit economics given seasonal peaks.
- Security: must support SSO (SAML) and audit logs; data residency not required today but wanted retention controls.
- Model preferences: open to curated open models if performance/cost match, but preference expressed for established brand (OpenAI) for risk reduction.

Why lost to OpenAI/Anthropic (notes from procurement + execs):
- "We want the simplest integration path to ship before peak season." (Procurement quote)
- Perception that OpenAI offers lower friction (familiar SDKs, existing team experience).
- AmberCore had trial credits and some initial bench tests with OpenAI; procurement flagged time-to-prod advantage.
- Internal champion left (Lead PM) and replacement prioritized vendor with minimal ops overhead.
- Pricing: Redwood's dedicated/reserved options attractive for cost at scale, but AmberCore feared commitment complexity vs pay-as-you-go OpenAI.

What we tried:
- Detailed cost modeling vs expected traffic (showed potential 18% savings at scale with Dedicated).
- POC with hosted instance and workload benchmarks. Replied to security questionnaire quickly and offered canary plan.
- Proposal included staged rollout to reduce commitment.

Open items and follow-ups for nurture:
- Capture post-selection feedback: invite them to a benchmark workshop (offer to reproduce their OpenAI tests).
- Send one-page comparison focused on time-to-prod mitigations (starter SDKs, rollout templates).
- Monitor for churn signal after peak season — possible re-engagement window.

Next internal actions:
- AE Jordan to send post-mortem to account team and product feedback to PS/research (due 2025-11-10).
- Add AmberCore to 6-month nurture cadence; include benchmarking invite and new-starter credits offer.

CRM shorthand / fragments:
- Closed-lost -> OpenAI direct. Brand + credits trumped Dedicated economics.
- No legal/regulatory blocker (would consider Private later), main issue operational speed and internal champion.
- Keep on mid-market nurture list; high re-engagement probability after peak season.
